title.value: New Insights on Reducing Abrupt Representation Change in Online Continual Learning
title.justification: The title clearly reflects the focus of the paper which is on addressing abrupt representation changes in the online continual learning scenario.
title.quote: N EW I NSIGHTS ON R EDUCING A BRUPT R EPRESENTATION C HANGE IN O NLINE C ONTINUAL L EARNING

extractions.description: This paper addresses the challenge of abrupt representation change in online continual learning. It discusses the limitations of Experience Replay (ER) in handling new classes and proposes new methods such as ER-Asymmetric Cross-Entropy (ER-ACE) and ER-Asymmetric Metric Learning (ER-AML) to stabilize representation updates. The paper evaluates these methods on standard benchmarks demonstrating their effectiveness and computational efficiency.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the technical aspects of continual learning and representation updates rather than addressing climate or ecological sustainable development directly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In the online continual learning paradigm, agents must learn from a changing distribution while respecting memory and compute constraints.

primary_category.justification: As the paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development, it does not fit into any primary category related to these areas.
primary_category.quote: Continual learning is concerned with building models that can learn and accumulate knowledge and skills over time.

secondary_categories.justification: The main focus of the paper is on continual learning methodologies, which do not directly relate to climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose a new method which mitigates this issue by shielding the learned representations from drastic adaptation to accommodate new classes.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific sub-category within the climate or ecological sustainable development spectrum.
primary_sub_category.quote: The main challenge is to design models that can learn how to use the new data and acquire new knowledge, while preserving or improving the performance on previously learned data.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories are relevant as the paper focuses on continual learning, not aligned with climate or ecological sectors.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We direct our attention to the representations being learned and investigate how the features of previously learned classes change and drift over time.

applications.justification: The applications discussed relate to continual learning and computational efficiency rather than specific climate or ecological sustainability applications.
applications.quote: Empirical results show significant gains over strong baselines on standard continual learning benchmarks.

new_primary_category.justification: All discussed topics revolve around continual learning technologies, which do not require the suggestion of a new climate or ecological sustainable development category.
new_primary_category.quote: We have highlighted the issue of abrupt representation change when new classes are introduced.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The continual learning domain does not require a new sub-category under climate or environmental sustainability.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a new family of methods addressing this issue by treating incoming and past data asymmetrically.
